verification: Exp 39 interpretation control: random init vs trained
verdict: REVISED INTERPRETATION: random init has MORE spectral variance than the trained model. Training on natural language REMOVES the variance that initialization provides. The bridge hypothesis (random keys ~ quasi-random frames, mostly collapsed) holds at init; training pushes to FULLY collapsed. The 'exposure law' is correct in direction but the baseline was wrong: it's not 'exposure creates collapse from variance' but 'exposure completes the collapse that init only starts'.
